To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the VAE can be used to reconstruct 3D objects with varying levels of noise, 2) the PVAE can be used for classification and prediction of 3D object segments, and 3) the LVAE can be applied to classification and prediction of object segments with partial input.

1) VAE architectures are capable of repairing complex, varied noises; 2) the VAE architecture is capable of learning latent spaces for object in-fills and de-noising; 3) the LVAE and PVAE architectures are capable of learning latent representations of object segments for classification and prediction; 4) voxel models are computationally prohibitive for learning structured 3D filters, and; 5) voxel models are visually complex and difficult to interpret.
the VAE is a powerful tool for object reconstruction, classification, and prediction, and that the LVAE and PVAE are novel extensions to the VAE that can improve its performance in these tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of unsupervised object classification and prediction in 3D through semantic sampling.
the development of a novel 3D object classification and prediction framework, and the use of VAEs to perform object reconstruction and de-noising tasks.
the use of variational reconstruction architectures in the context of 3D object classification, prediction, and reconstruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

although the use of voxel representations for 3D object classification and prediction is interesting and potentially useful for certain tasks, the computational complexity, massive data sparsity and lack of descriptiveness of the voxel representations are major obstacles to the development of high-performance 3D object reconstruction networks.
the proposed methods for unsupervised object reconstruction are promising, but that further investigation is required.

although the proposed VAE architectures have the potential for use in 3D reconstruction tasks, their performance is still limited by the lack of high level 3D filters and by the sparsity of voxel models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of variational auto-encoders in 3D object segmentation is an interesting area of research that is still in its infancy, and that further investigation of this field is needed to determine the full potential of this technology.
the LVAE and PVAE architectures are capable of learning a semantic latent space for classification and prediction of 3D object segments.

the use of 3D VAEs is an exciting and novel approach to the problem of object in-filling, but that the use of more complex architectures and more advanced loss functions is required for more complex and varied input data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VAE is a powerful tool in the field of unsupervised 3D object classification and prediction.
the latent space of a variational auto-encoder can be used for object classification and prediction, even when the input is only a partial, semantically sampled object.
we have shown that VAE architectures can be used for unsupervised object classification and prediction, even with partial input samples and varying input quality.
